A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the VMR in the aquifer is low, but the VMR is high in the viral population, suggesting a PtP strategy.

the PtP mechanism is a new and previously unrecognized fundamental microbial strategy that occurs in all microbial communities and is a significant contributor to the KtW and PtW viral strategies, and that it can be triggered by persistent pollutants that provide a long-term carbon source.
the PtP strategy occurs when a long-term carbon source is present, which alters the carbon cycle, resulting in a shift to a PtP strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
viruses can be more than simply the agents of cell death and that their interactions with the environment and with their hosts are more complex and nuanced than previously appreciated.
the VMR, a key metric of the virus-microbial interaction, can be influenced by the nature of the carbon sources and that this has a major influence on the structure of the microbial community.
we propose a novel mechanism for the control of microbial community structure in aquifers, and we suggest that this PtP process is widespread in the subsurface.
